claims.statement: For the frozen ordinary-tree definitions, S(T,p)=A_p(T,p)-A_(p-1)(T,p), where A_k sums, with distinct original leaf tags, independent k-sets of H_v meeting N_T(s_v)\{v} over v in F_p(T). The selector Delta_p(T-v)<0 decomposes as Delta_p(H_v)+Delta_(p-1)(R_v)<0, which does not itself give the required sign for the previous-rank difference Delta_(p-1)(H_v)-Delta_(p-1)(R_v). The universal aggregate implication and an eligible positive counterexample both remain unresolved by this result.
claims.scope: Exact combinatorial identity and unresolved sign bridge for finite ordinary trees with p=alpha(T)-2 and x(T)+2<=p; no residual hypothesis.
claims.reason: Partition independent sets of H_v by whether they meet W_v=N_T(s_v)\{v}; use I_(T-v)=I_H+z I_R. The resulting selector and summand differences compare different adjacent ranks with opposing signs, leaving exactly A_p<=A_(p-1) to prove or refute.

limitations: The exact identity does not establish the required aggregate sign or produce a counterexample.
The T_m checks cover only m=75, 100, 150 at p=alpha-2 and are not universal evidence.
No Lean build or complete tree census was performed.
The independent-set polynomial evaluator is a copied admitted evaluator; its first-descent routine was not used, and the runner scans through the terminal rank as required.
